content.title: Converting Fractions, Decimals, and Percentages
content.overview: This lesson focuses on the fluid conversion between three ways of representing the same value: fractions, decimals, and percentages. Mastering these conversions is essential for comparing magnitudes and solving word problems on the ACT.
learning_objectives: Convert decimals to percentages by shifting the decimal point.
Convert fractions to decimals and then to percentages.
Convert percentages back to decimals or fractions.
Verify the magnitude of converted values to avoid common placement errors.

sections.title: The Shift-and-Label Strategy
sections.content: To convert a decimal to a percentage, you multiply the decimal by 100. In practice, this means moving the decimal point two places to the right and attaching the percent symbol (%). For example, 0.45 becomes 45%. If the decimal has fewer than two places, add a placeholder zero (e.g., 0.8 becomes 80%).

sections.title: Converting Fractions to Percentages
sections.content:
When starting with a fraction, the first step is to convert it into a decimal. Divide the numerator (top number) by the denominator (bottom number). Once you have the decimal result, apply the Shift-and-Label strategy by moving the decimal point two places to the right.

![A flow chart showing the steps: Fraction, Divide, Decimal, Shift Right 2 Places, Percent.](https://img.justsolvely.com/followUpImage/92d86336-0dcb-4454-a822-598fd2ace358-1786505449195-462.webp)

sections.title: Reversing the Process
sections.content: To convert a percentage back to a decimal, perform the inverse operation: divide by 100. This involves moving the decimal point two places to the left and removing the percent sign. For example, 7% becomes 0.07. To convert a percentage to a fraction, place the percentage value over 100 and simplify (e.g., 25% = 25/100 = 1/4).

worked_examples.question: Express the fraction 5/8 as a percentage.
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: Convert the fraction to a decimal by dividing 5 by 8. 5 ÷ 8 = 0.625. Step 2: Move the decimal point two places to the right. 0.625 becomes 62.5. Step 3: Attach the percent sign. The result is 62.5%.

worked_examples.question: What is 0.004 expressed as a percentage?
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: Identify the decimal 0.004. Step 2: Move the decimal point two places to the right. 0.004 → 0.04. Step 3: Attach the percent sign. The result is 0.4%.

common_mistakes: Moving the decimal point only one place instead of two (e.g., thinking 0.5 is 5%).
Moving the decimal in the wrong direction when converting from decimal to percent.
Forgetting to add placeholder zeros when the decimal has fewer than two digits (e.g., 0.2 becoming 2% instead of 20%).
exam_tips: Always perform a sanity check: if the original number is greater than 1, the percentage must be greater than 100%.
Memorize common conversions like 1/8 = 0.125 = 12.5% and 2/3 ≈ 0.667 = 66.7% to save time.
If you are stuck, remember that 'percent' literally means 'per one hundred'.
content.recap: To convert to a percentage, multiply by 100 (shift decimal two places right). To convert from a percentage, divide by 100 (shift decimal two places left). Always ensure the magnitude remains consistent across forms.

knowledge_claims.content: To convert a decimal to a percentage, move the decimal point exactly two places to the right and add a percent sign.
To convert a fraction to a decimal, divide the numerator by the denominator.
A decimal value greater than 1 corresponds to a percentage greater than 100%.
A decimal value less than 0.01 corresponds to a percentage less than 1%.
To convert a percentage to a decimal, move the decimal point two places to the left and remove the percent sign.
Moving the decimal point only one place when converting a decimal to a percent results in a value that is ten times too small.
Verify a conversion by checking if the percent value equals the original decimal multiplied by 100.
When converting 0.8 to a percentage, a placeholder zero must be used to correctly shift the decimal two places, resulting in 80%.
The term 'percent' means 'per one hundred', which is why dividing a percentage by 100 converts it to its decimal form.
To convert a percentage to a fraction, place the numerical value of the percent over 100 and simplify the resulting fraction.
The decimal 0.375 is equivalent to 37.5% because 0.375 multiplied by 100 is 37.5.
The value 1/4 is equivalent to 0.25 and 25%.
